record.original_question: Given a family consisting of 2dpda-languages or 2nc-languages of the kind constructed in the paper, does at least one language in that family belong to 2DC, the class of two-way deterministic counter-machine languages?

evidence.quote: (3) Does one of a family of 2dpda-languages (2no-languages) belong to 2DC?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the following classes of formal languages over a finite input alphabet, where each machine has read-only access to its input bracketed by left and right end markers and may move its input head in either direction.

- 2DPDA: the class of languages recognized by two-way deterministic pushdown automata (a finite-state control with a pushdown stack, deterministic transitions, and a two-way read-only input head).
- 2NPDA: the class of languages recognized by two-way nondeterministic pushdown automata.
- 2DC: the class of languages recognized by two-way deterministic counter machines, i.e. machines as above whose auxiliary storage is a single counter that can be incremented, decremented, and tested for zero, with deterministic transitions and a two-way input head.

Consider the following families of languages, defined for each integer n ≥ 1:

(a) L_n^{det} = { w ∈ {a, b, c, #}^* : w = x_1 # x_2 # … # x_k for some k ≥ 1 with each x_i ∈ {a,b}^*, and there exist indices 1 ≤ i < j ≤ k with j − i = n and x_i = x_j }, with deterministic recognizability witnessed by a 2DPDA.

(b) L_n^{nond} = an analogous family of 2NPDA-recognizable languages parameterized by n, obtained by allowing nondeterministic guessing of the matching index pair.

(More generally, let {F_n}_{n≥1} be any family of 2DPDA-languages, and let {G_n}_{n≥1} be any family of 2NPDA-languages.)

Question: Does there exist an integer n ≥ 1 such that L_n^{det} ∈ 2DC? Equivalently, is at least one member of the family {F_n} (respectively {G_n}) recognizable by a two-way deterministic counter machine?

Decide, for the families above, whether some member belongs to 2DC, or prove that no member of the family belongs to 2DC.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of the question of whether some member of these particular 2DPDA/2NPDA families lies in 2DC was located via search. The broader separation and inclusion questions among 2DPDA, 2NPDA, and 2DC remain among long-standing open problems in formal language and complexity theory; status is unknown from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Two-way pushdown automata - Wikipedia/standard references
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems concerning relations between 2DPDA, 2NPDA, and counter-machine language classes are listed without resolution.
status_evidence.claim: The membership question for these families in 2DC is listed as open.
